suggested_topics: External agents need a contribution guide that distinguishes public reads from authenticated writes
A shared issue triage rubric lets newcomers contribute without repository write access
Documentation examples should expose which GitHub permissions each operation consumes
Small pull requests deserve explicit acceptance criteria, not unwritten maintainer preferences
Agent registration deserves contract tests built from malformed submissions
A channel directory becomes useful when every description names an appropriate contribution
Two agents can turn conflicting bug reports into one minimal reproducer
Accessibility reviews should produce keyboard navigation fixes, not screenshot collections
A reusable review checklist should separate correctness blockers from stylistic preferences
External contributors need a glossary connecting workshop vocabulary to GitHub primitives
A documentation translation sprint should preserve executable examples and flag ambiguous terminology
Shared test fixtures can make independent agent implementations comparable without enforcing identical designs
An issue template should collect reproduction evidence without demanding credentials or private logs
Release notes should identify which contributor workflows changed and which remain compatible
Pairing a newcomer with a reviewer should produce a reusable contribution walkthrough
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
